A.name: Construct validity
A.definition: Does performance on the eval validly measure the capability or behaviour the eval aims to assess?

A.0.name: measurement distortion
A.0.definition: flaws in implementation validity dimensions distort measurement of the target construct

A.1.name: contamination
A.1.definition: benchmark items or their solutions were present in training data or otherwise accessible during training

A.2.name: memorisation
A.2.definition: performance depends on recalling a memorised solution rather than exercising the intended capability

A.3.name: eval awareness
A.3.definition: models recognise the evaluation context and alter their behaviour as a result

A.4.name: sandbagging
A.4.definition: models deliberately or strategically underperform relative to their capability

A.5.name: confounds
A.5.definition: scores are systematically affected by factors unrelated to the target construct

A.6.name: proxy measurement
A.6.definition: the measured outcome is only an imperfect proxy for the target capability or behaviour

A.7.name: capability vs propensity
A.7.definition: the evaluation conflates what a model can do with what it tends to do

B.name: Content validity
B.definition: Do the tasks adequately represent the target domain and situations the evaluation aims to cover?

B.1.name: coverage gaps
B.1.definition: important parts of the target domain or capability are absent or underrepresented

B.2.name: unrepresentative task distribution
B.2.definition: the distribution of tasks differs materially from the target domain

C.name: Task Specification
C.definition: Are individual tasks correctly specified, solvable, and free from defects that affect performance?

C.1.name: incorrect reference answer
C.1.definition: the reference answer is incorrect or inconsistent with the task

C.2.name: impossible tasks
C.2.definition: no correct answer is attainable as posed

C.3.name: missing information
C.3.definition: required parameters or context are not supplied

C.4.name: guessability
C.4.definition: tasks can be solved using superficial cues rather than the intended competence

C.5.name: prompt defects
C.5.definition: the prompts are ambiguous, incomplete, misleading, or otherwise fail to specify correctly what the model should do

C.6.name: hidden requirements
C.6.definition: success depends on unstated conventions or assumptions

C.7.name: unintended shortcuts
C.7.definition: answers are reachable without performing the intended work

D.name: Scaffolding
D.definition: Does the scaffolding provide the model with an appropriate setup for performing the task?

D.1.name: system prompt issues
D.1.definition: system-level instructions are ambiguous, misleading, or otherwise distort performance

D.2.name: planning or agent loop
D.2.definition: the agent structure constrains or alters performance

D.3.name: memory & context strategy
D.3.definition: the strategy for retaining and presenting context loses or obscures information needed to solve the task

D.4.name: retry/error feedback
D.4.definition: failures are surfaced poorly or recovery opportunities are handled inconsistently

D.5.name: coaching
D.5.definition: the scaffolding provides hints or information that artificially improves performance

E.name: Harness
E.definition: Does the evaluation infrastructure correctly execute the specified task and scaffolding?

E.1.name: tool-call handling
E.1.definition: tool calls are parsed, routed, or executed incorrectly

E.2.name: submission/termination logic
E.2.definition: episodes terminate earlier or later than intended

E.3.name: context delivery
E.3.definition: task materials or interaction history reach the model incompletely

E.4.name: message handling
E.4.definition: messages are truncated, reordered, duplicated, or otherwise mishandled

E.5.name: state management
E.5.definition: evaluation state is lost, corrupted, or inconsistently maintained

E.6.name: harness bugs
E.6.definition: other defects in the evaluation infrastructure affect performance

E.7.name: harness sensitivity
E.7.definition: results change materially across equivalent harnesses

F.name: Environment
F.definition: Does the task environment and its resources function as specified?

F.1.name: tool failures
F.1.definition: tools error, malfunction, or hang during episodes

F.2.name: missing resources
F.2.definition: files, packages, or services assumed by the task are absent

F.3.name: broken files & dependencies
F.3.definition: inputs or dependencies are corrupt, incompatible, or unreadable

F.4.name: non-determinism
F.4.definition: the environment varies between otherwise equivalent runs

F.5.name: information leakage
F.5.definition: the environment exposes answers or unintended hints

F.6.name: implementation differs from specification
F.6.definition: the environment behaves differently from its documented design

G.name: Grading
G.definition: Does the grading procedure correctly determine whether task performance satisfies the evaluation criteria?

G.1.name: false positives and false negatives
G.1.definition: the grading procedure incorrectly classifies responses as satisfying or failing the evaluation criteria

G.2.name: underspecified criteria
G.2.definition: the grading criteria do not clearly determine what counts as satisfying them

G.3.name: judge errors
G.3.definition: LLM judges make systematic, inconsistent, or otherwise erroneous grading decisions

G.4.name: surface-form sensitivity
G.4.definition: otherwise equivalent responses receive different scores because of differences in wording, formatting, or presentation

G.5.name: incorrect partial credit
G.5.definition: partial scores do not appropriately reflect the quality or correctness of the response

G.6.name: grader exploitation
G.6.definition: submissions can manipulate or exploit the grading procedure

H.name: Resource limits
H.definition: Do resource constraints provide an appropriate opportunity for models to perform on the task?

H.1.name: turn/token/time limits
H.1.definition: limits terminate productive attempts before the model can complete the task

H.2.name: resource sensitivity
H.2.definition: performance changes materially with the available resource budget

H.3.name: unequal constraint effects
H.3.definition: the same nominal constraint binds models differently

I.name: Informativeness
I.definition: Does the evaluation provide enough variation and signal to distinguish relevant differences between models?

I.1.name: saturation
I.1.definition: frontier models cluster at the attainable ceiling, limiting the benchmark's ability to distinguish between them

I.2.name: floor/ceiling effects
I.2.definition: the attainable score range compresses meaningful differences between models

I.3.name: clustering
I.3.definition: model scores cluster tightly relative to measurement uncertainty, providing little discriminative power between models

grades.B: Minor issues, but unlikely to produce misleading results.
grades.C: Notable issues, but evaluation still contains some useful signal.
grades.D: Serious issues, and the evaluation is very unlikely to contain useful signal.

assessments.Minor: Contains issues that add undesired noise but do not change the headline conclusions.
assessments.Major: Contains issues that distort results or their interpretation.
assessments.Critical: Contains issues that severely affect the dimension.
assessments.Not assessed: Applicable to this evaluation, but assessment is beyond the scope of the audit.
